text: The function concerned with converting inputs into outputs of goods and services is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Production management transforms inputs into valuable outputs.

text: The system that produces standardised goods in large volume is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Mass production makes large volumes of standardised products.

text: The production of goods one at a time to customer specification is called
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Job production makes unique items to order.

text: Production management and operations management are entirely different concepts
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Operations management is the broader term that includes services as well as goods.

text: List the objectives of production management
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Right quality right quantity right time and minimum cost.
explanation: These objectives ensure efficient and customer satisfying production.

text: Explain the scope of production and operations management
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: The scope covers product design process planning plant location and layout production planning and control quality and maintenance management.
explanation: Cover the activities from design to control and improvement.

text: The decision about where to set up a plant is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Plant location chooses the site for the production facility.

text: The physical arrangement of machines and departments within a plant is the plant
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Plant layout arranges facilities for efficient flow of work.

text: A product layout is best suited for continuous mass production
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Product layout arranges machines in the sequence of operations for mass output.

text: List the factors affecting plant location
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Nearness to raw materials market transport labour power and government incentives.
explanation: These factors influence the cost and convenience of a site.

text: Explain the types of plant layout
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Layouts include product layout process layout fixed position layout and cellular layout each suited to different types of production and volume.
explanation: Describe each layout and the production setting it suits.

text: The process of deciding what when and how much to produce is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Production planning determines what and how much to produce and when.

text: The document that lists the materials and operations required to make a product is the
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: The bill of materials details all components needed for a product.

text: Routing determines the sequence of operations for a job
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Routing fixes the path and sequence of operations for production.

text: List the steps in production planning and control
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Routing scheduling dispatching and follow up.
explanation: These steps plan and control the flow of production.

text: Explain the importance of production planning and control
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Production planning and control ensures optimum use of resources timely delivery reduced costs and smooth workflow by planning scheduling and monitoring production.
explanation: Cover resource use delivery and cost benefits.

text: The function that ensures materials are available in the right quantity at the right time is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Materials management handles procurement storage and issue of materials.

text: The level of inventory at which a new order must be placed is the
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: The reorder level triggers replenishment before stock runs out.

text: Total quality management makes quality the responsibility of every employee
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: TQM involves everyone in continuous improvement of quality.

text: List the techniques of inventory control
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: ABC analysis economic order quantity reorder level and just in time.
explanation: These techniques balance inventory cost with availability.

text: Explain the objectives of quality management
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Quality management aims to meet customer requirements prevent defects reduce waste and improve reliability through standards inspection and continuous improvement.
explanation: Cover customer satisfaction and defect prevention.

text: The function that keeps machines and equipment in working condition is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Maintenance keeps plant and machinery in good working order.

text: Maintenance carried out before a breakdown occurs is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Preventive maintenance is scheduled to avoid breakdowns.

text: Work study combines method study and work measurement
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Work study analyses methods and measures work to improve efficiency.

text: List the types of maintenance
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Breakdown preventive predictive and corrective maintenance.
explanation: These approaches differ in when maintenance is performed.

text: Explain the objectives of work study
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Work study improves productivity by eliminating waste simplifying methods and setting fair time standards for planning and incentives.
explanation: Cover method improvement and standard setting.

text: The philosophy of producing only what is needed when it is needed is
subject: Production and Operations Management
options: Just in time|Mass production|Batch production|Job production
explanation: Just in time minimises inventory by producing to demand.

text: The network of organisations involved in producing and delivering a product is the supply
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: The supply chain links suppliers producers and distributors.

text: Lean production aims to eliminate waste in all forms
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Lean production continuously removes non value adding activities.

text: List the benefits of just in time production
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Lower inventory reduced waste better quality and faster response to demand.
explanation: JIT cuts costs and improves responsiveness.

text: Explain the objectives of supply chain management
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Supply chain management coordinates suppliers producers and distributors to reduce cost improve service and respond quickly to customers.
explanation: Cover cost service and responsiveness objectives.

text: Assertion: Just in time reduces inventory holding costs. Reason: JIT produces only when demand arises so stock levels stay low
subject: Production and Operations Management
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion|Both are true but reason does not explain assertion|Assertion is true but reason is false|Assertion is false but reason is true
explanation: Low stock from demand driven production directly cuts holding costs.

text: Match the concept to its focus
subject: Production and Operations Management
options: JIT - minimise inventory|Supply chain - reduce quality|Lean - increase waste|Quality - ignore customers
explanation: JIT minimises inventory while lean eliminates waste and quality satisfies customers.

text: The annual demand is 12000 units and each order costs 200. The economic order quantity with holding cost 3 per unit is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: EOQ equals the square root of two times demand times ordering cost divided by holding cost so square root of two times 12000 times 200 divided by 3 equals about 1265 units.

text: The time taken by a worker to complete a job is studied in
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Time study measures the time required to perform a task.

text: The study of the movements of workers to eliminate unnecessary motion is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Motion study improves methods by removing wasteful movements.

text: Explain the factors determining the choice of production system
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: The choice depends on product variety volume customer specification and capital requirements with job batch and mass systems suiting different combinations.
explanation: Relate product volume and variety to the production system.

text: Read the case: A garment factory receives large orders for many different styles. Recommend the most suitable production system and justify it
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Batch production is best because it handles moderate volumes of many product styles in runs switching between them efficiently.
explanation: Match the variety and volume to batch production.

text: Read the case: A plant faces frequent machine breakdowns that halt production. Recommend a maintenance strategy to reduce downtime
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: The plant should adopt preventive and predictive maintenance with scheduled inspections and monitoring to fix problems before they cause breakdowns.
explanation: Propose planned maintenance to replace reactive repairs.

text: A factory produces 5000 units in 50 hours. Its production rate per hour is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Production rate equals output divided by time so 5000 divided by 50 equals 100 units per hour.

text: Explain the importance of plant location
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Plant location affects cost of raw materials and distribution availability of labour and utilities and long term profitability so it is a strategic and hard to reverse decision.
explanation: Cover cost labour and long term impact of location.

text: Capacity refers to the maximum output a plant can produce in a period
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Capacity is the maximum sustainable output per period.

text: Explain the techniques of quality control
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Quality control uses inspection statistical quality control control charts and acceptance sampling to detect and correct defects and maintain standards.
explanation: Cover inspection and statistical techniques of quality control.

text: The classification of inventory items into A B and C categories by value is
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: ABC analysis focuses control on the high value A items.

text: Explain the difference between product and process layout
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Product layout arranges machines by the sequence of operations while process layout groups similar machines together by function.
explanation: Product layout suits mass production and process layout suits variety.

text: Explain the steps in purchasing procedure
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Purchasing proceeds from identifying the need through supplier selection placing the order receiving and inspecting goods to payment and record keeping.
explanation: Trace the purchasing cycle from requisition to payment.

text: A lead time is the gap between placing an order and receiving the goods
subject: Production and Operations Management
explanation: Lead time is the delay between ordering and delivery.

text: Explain the importance of materials management
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Materials management ensures uninterrupted production at minimum cost by buying storing and issuing materials efficiently and controlling inventory.
explanation: Cover availability cost and inventory control.

text: List the objectives of maintenance management
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Minimise breakdowns reduce downtime extend equipment life and ensure safety.
explanation: These objectives keep production running smoothly.

text: Explain the benefits and limitations of automation
subject: Production and Operations Management
correctAnswer: Automation raises speed consistency and quality and lowers unit cost but requires high capital and skilled staff and reduces flexibility.
explanation: Balance productivity gains against cost and flexibility.
